method: Availability is the share of a period a service is usable, so a target of p percent leaves (100 - p)/100 of the period for outages. With a fixed period of P hours the allowed downtime is (1 - p/100) * P * 3600 seconds, the achieved availability after an observed downtime d is (1 - d / (P * 3600)) * 100 percent, the share of the budget used is d divided by the allowed downtime times 100, and the budget left is the allowed downtime minus d. The periods are the fixed lengths the page lists: a day is 24 h, a week 168 h, a month 730 h, a quarter 2190 h and a year 8760 h, so months and years divide evenly and a quarter is three months. The nines shorthand counts the 9s in the target, which is the nearest whole number to minus the base-10 logarithm of the shortfall (100 - p)/100, reported only when that logarithm is a whole number from one to six, so 99.9 percent is three nines and 99.9999 percent is six. Allowed and remaining seconds are rounded to 0.01, the achieved availability to 0.0001 percent and the share of the budget to 0.1 percent. Targets greater than 0 and at most 99.9999 percent are accepted, downtime greater than or equal to 0 and at most the length of the period in minutes is accepted and may be left blank, and the period must be one of the listed keys. Text, exponent notation, a blank or out-of-range target, an unknown period, negative downtime and downtime longer than the period are refused with the exact reason, and decimal commas are accepted. Downtime above the budget is reported as an overrun with a warning rather than refused. This is arithmetic on the target and the downtime you supply: it does not measure availability, does not decide how partial failures are counted, and treats planned maintenance as downtime. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Availability is the fraction of a period a service is usable, so an n percent target leaves (100 - n)/100 of the period available for outages.
The nines shorthand counts the 9s in the target: 99.9 percent is three nines and 99.99 percent is four, and each extra nine divides the allowed downtime by ten.
Availability budgets are usually quoted over fixed period lengths, with a month taken as 730 hours and a year as 8760 hours so the figures are reproducible.
